title: Furmint
description: Tokaj's grape: searing acidity, noble rot and smoky, mineral dry wines.
L: Furmint gives whites with very high acidity and flavours of lemon, green apple, quince, pear, smoke and a mineral, flinty edge. With age or botrytis, honey, apricot and marmalade appear. Body ranges from medium to full; alcohol can be high in dry styles.

Furmint is Hungary's signature grape, probably native to the Tokaj region; it's also grown in Slovenia as Šipon. It ripens late, which keeps acidity high. Its thin skins become thinner as it ripens, making it highly susceptible to noble rot, Botrytis cinerea. That's why it's the main grape of Tokaji Aszú.
Why is Furmint so suited to noble rot?
Its skins thin as it ripens

Dry Furmint is pale lemon, with citrus, quince and smoky, flinty notes, high acidity and a firm, mineral palate. Sweet Tokaji is gold to amber, with apricot, marmalade and honey, balanced by vivid acidity. That acidity is the common thread.
Not true. Its very high acidity is its signature.
Furmint has very high acidity, with quince and smoke
It's native to Tokaj and susceptible to noble rot
Its acidity links dry and sweet styles
Name other places that grow it

Furmint covers about 60 to 70% of Tokaj's vineyards, in north-east Hungary. The region's volcanic soils, from clay and loess to rhyolite and andesite, give mineral, smoky wines. The Bodrog and Tisza rivers create autumn mists, ideal for noble rot. Hárslevelű and Sárgamuskotály, a Muscat, are its partners.

Furmint also grows in Somló, a tiny Hungarian volcanic hill known for powerful dry whites, and in Slovenia, as Šipon, in Štajerska. Austria's Burgenland, around Rust, has revived it. Small plantings exist in Croatia, South Africa and California.
Match each place or name to Furmint.
Furmint is Hungary's grape, with neighbours.
Tokaj's soils change from hill to hill. Furmint from rhyolite tends to be more mineral and lean; from loess, rounder and fruitier.
What creates the mists that help noble rot in Tokaj?
The two rivers meet at Tokaj, bringing autumn mists.

Explain how Tokaji Aszú is made

Aszú berries are individually picked, botrytised and shrivelled, almost raisins. They're stored as a paste, then soaked in fermenting must or a base wine for 12 to 60 hours, which extracts sugar and flavour. The mix is pressed and fermented slowly, then aged in small Gönci barrels in cold, damp cellars.
Botrytised berries soaked in base wine

Sweetness was measured in puttonyos: the number of 25 kg baskets, called puttony, of aszú berries added to a 136-litre Gönci barrel of base wine. From 3 to 6 puttonyos. Since 2013, Tokaji Aszú must have at least 120 g/l of sugar, equal to the old 5 puttonyos, and the term puttonyos is optional.
Baskets of aszú berries per barrel
The number of 25 kg baskets added to a 136-litre barrel.

Eszencia is the free-run juice that drips from aszú berries under their own weight. It can contain over 450 g/l of sugar, ferments for years and rarely exceeds 5% alcohol. It's one of the rarest, sweetest wines in the world, traditionally served by the spoon.
Over 450 g/l, served by the spoon
Put the making of Tokaji Aszú in order.
Soak in base wine or must
Selection, soaking and slow fermentation give Aszú its depth.
Aszú berries are soaked in base wine, then fermented slowly
Since 2013, Aszú needs at least 120 g/l of sugar
Eszencia is free-run juice with over 450 g/l

Since the early 2000s, Tokaj producers have made more dry Furmint, partly because botrytis doesn't come every year, and partly to show the grape's quality. Dry Furmint has high acidity, citrus, quince, pear, smoky and mineral notes, and can be rich and textured, often compared with white Burgundy or Chenin Blanc.

Dry Furmint comes from healthy, non-botrytised grapes, often from single vineyards, called dűlő. Some ferment in oak, which adds texture; others in steel for purity. Its acidity lets it age 10 years or more. Producers like Királyudvar, Oremus and Szepsy helped establish its reputation.
Dry Furmint is made from healthy grapes without noble rot.
Yes. Botrytised grapes are kept for sweet wines.

Tokaj's vineyards were classified from 1730, among the first in the world, into first, second and third class. Single-vineyard names like Szent Tamás, Betsek and Mézes Mály are used again on labels, especially for dry Furmint, like Burgundy's crus.
What is a dűlő in Tokaj?
Dűlő names, like Szent Tamás, mark single vineyards.
Dry Furmint has grown since the 2000s
It's made from healthy grapes, often single vineyards

Dry Furmint's acidity and texture suit rich fish, roast chicken, pork, goose, and creamy Hungarian dishes like chicken paprikash. Its smoky, mineral side suits smoked fish and mushrooms. Serve at 10 to 12 degrees.

Aszú suits foie gras, blue cheese, fruit tarts, apricot desserts and even spicy Asian food. Its acidity keeps it fresh with rich food. Serve at 10 to 12 degrees. It ages for decades: Aszú from the 18th century has been found still drinkable.
Foie gras, blue cheese, apricot tarts
Match each Furmint wine to a pairing.
Furmint offers a wine for many courses.
Louis XIV is said to have called Tokaji the wine of kings and the king of wines. It was served at European courts for centuries.
Dry Furmint suits paprikash, pork and smoked fish
Aszú suits foie gras, blue cheese and fruit desserts
Both are served at 10 to 12 degrees and age well
